blocks.prompt: 18 Find the general solution of the differential equation \(x\frac{dy}{dx} - y = \frac{x^4 + x^3y}{y^3 - x^3}\).
blocks.explanation:
Putting \(y = vx\) turns the right side into \(x\) times a function of \(v\), and the left side into \(x^2\frac{dv}{dx}\), so the equation is homogeneous.
We must find the general solution.
Plan: substitute \(y = vx\), separate, divide \(v^3 - 1\) by \(v + 1\), integrate, put back \(v\).
steps:
Given: \(x\frac{dy}{dx} - y = \frac{x^4 + x^3y}{y^3 - x^3}\).
To find: the general solution.
Method: Homogeneous equation: substitute \(y = vx\), \(\frac{dy}{dx} = v + x\frac{dv}{dx}\). (Dividing by \(x\) gives \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y}{x} + \frac{1 + y/x}{(y/x)^3 - 1}\), a function of \(y/x\) only.)

Left side with \(y = vx\)
\[x\left(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right) - vx = x^2\dfrac{dv}{dx}\]
Why: the terms \(xv\) and \(-vx\) cancel.

Right side with \(y = vx\)
\[\dfrac{x^4 + x^4v}{x^3v^3 - x^3} = \dfrac{x^4(1 + v)}{x^3(v^3 - 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{x(1 + v)}{v^3 - 1}\]
Why: \(x^3y = x^3 \cdot vx = x^4v\) and \(y^3 = v^3x^3\); then cancel \(x^3\).

Equate and separate
\[x^2\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{x(1 + v)}{v^3 - 1}\]
\[\dfrac{v^3 - 1}{v + 1}\,dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}\]
Why: divide both sides by \(x\), then move \(v\)-terms to \(dv\) and \(x\)-terms to \(dx\).

Divide \(v^3 - 1\) by \(v + 1\)
\[(v + 1)(v^2 - v + 1) = v^3 + 1\]
\[\dfrac{v^3 - 1}{v + 1} = v^2 - v + 1 - \dfrac{2}{v + 1}\]
Why: \(v^3 - 1 = (v^3 + 1) - 2\). The degree of the numerator is higher, so we divide before integrating.

Integrate
\[\dfrac{v^3}{3} - \dfrac{v^2}{2} + v - 2\ln|v + 1|\]
\[= \ln|x| + \ln|C|\]
Why: power rule for each power of \(v\), and \(\int \frac{dv}{v + 1} = \ln|v + 1|\).

Multiply by 6 and collect the logs
\[2v^3 - 3v^2 + 6v\]
\[= 6\ln|x| + 12\ln|v + 1| + 6\ln|C|\]
\[= 6\ln|Cx(v + 1)^2|\]
Why: \(12\ln|v + 1| = 6\ln(v + 1)^2\), then \(\ln a + \ln b = \ln ab\).

Put back \(v = y/x\)
\[x(v + 1)^2 = \dfrac{(x + y)^2}{x}\]
\[\dfrac{2y^3}{x^3} - \dfrac{3y^2}{x^2} + \dfrac{6y}{x}\]
\[= 6\ln\left|\dfrac{C(x + y)^2}{x}\right|\]
Why: \(v + 1 = \frac{x + y}{x}\), so \(x(v + 1)^2 = x\cdot\frac{(x + y)^2}{x^2}\).

Multiply by \(x^3\)
\[2y^3 - 3xy^2 + 6x^2y\]
\[= 6x^3\ln\left|\dfrac{C(x + y)^2}{x}\right|\]
Why: this removes all fractions on the left.

Check
The derivative of the left side of the integrated equation is \(v^2 - v + 1 - \frac{2}{v + 1}\), which is the separated integrand \(\checkmark\). Differentiating the final answer implicitly (done with a computer algebra system) gives back \(x\frac{dy}{dx} - y = \frac{x^4 + x^3y}{y^3 - x^3}\) \(\checkmark\)
Why: both checks confirm the solution of the printed equation.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key (printed as number 21, not 18) gives \(2y^3 - 3xy^2 + 6x^2y = 6x^3\ln|C(y + x)|\). This does not satisfy the equation as printed. It is the solution when the denominator is \(y^3\) instead of \(y^3 - x^3\): then \(x\frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{1 + v}{v^3}\), \(\frac{v^3}{v + 1} = v^2 - v + 1 - \frac{1}{v + 1}\), and integration gives \(2v^3 - 3v^2 + 6v = 6\ln|Cx(v + 1)|\), which is the key's answer. So either the printed denominator or the key is wrong. For the question as printed (denominator \(y^3 - x^3\)) the correct answer is the one found above. (The keys are numbered 2 to 29 for 25 questions; the extra keys 15, 19 and 27 match no printed question.)
